title: Does GPS Need Internet? How Your Phone Finds You Offline
caption: GPS works without internet: your phone only listens to satellites and times their signals. Mobile data just speeds up the first fix and loads the map.
pinned_comment: Did you think GPS needed mobile data? 👇

lines.text: Your phone never talks to GPS satellites.
It only listens. That's why GPS works without internet.
About thirty GPS satellites circle the Earth, twenty thousand kilometers up.
Each one constantly broadcasts its position and the exact time from an atomic clock.
That signal needs about seven hundredths of a second to reach you.
Your phone compares the arrival times from at least four satellites.
A delay of one millionth of a second means an error of three hundred meters.
And here's the wild part: the satellite clocks run fast because of Einstein's relativity.
Weaker gravity speeds their clocks up, their speed slows them down.
Overall, they gain thirty-eight millionths of a second a day.
So engineers set them to tick slightly slower before launch.
The internet only helps your phone start faster and load the map.
So, does GPS need the internet? No. Your phone never talks to the satellites…

sources.title: Ohio State University (R. Pogge): GPS and Relativity
